text.p: The government suspended privatisation of Russia's biggest insurer OAO Rosgosstrakh, an official at the State Property Committee, which controls privatisation, said on Friday.
"Yesterday (State Property Committee Chairman Alfred) Kokh signed a regulation on cancelling a previous regulation on Rosgosstrakh's privatisation," Kokh's privatisation secretary told Reuters.

She gave no more details of the regulation. Under the Rosgosstrakh privatisation project, employees bought 20 percent of shares and a management team has a priority right for a further 30 percent. The remaining 50 percent were to be sold this year at an auction at 500 roubles (8 cents) per share with a face value of two roubles.

Rosgosstrakh's sale was one of the government biggest 1997 privatisation projects, together with the sales of Svyazinvest telecoms holding, Rosneft oil company and national power company Unified Energy System .

But the plan came under fire from the State Duma lower house of parliament, which considered the price of the sale too cheap. It asked an independent Audit Chamber to check the plan. The chamber found massive legal violations in the project and sent documents to the Prosecutor General's Office.
Rosgosstrakh's authorised capital based on 1994 calculations is 2.1 billion roubles ($364,000) at current exchage rates.
